note: Three selective SYK inhibitors reached Phase 2 in RA: MK-8457 matched its rat arthritis prediction in MTX-IR patients but was stopped for serious infections no model foresaw; cevidoplenib cleared mouse K/BxN arthritis yet missed DAS28, and lanraplenib missed the same endpoint with only a lupus model published. Fostamatinib is not a member of this class table and is not scored.
label: Rheumatoid arthritis (SYK)

engagement.confidence_note: Opening date is a proxy: first-in-human dosing began 2011 (NCT01446003), so the rat work predates it. ACR 2014 meeting abstract (Arthritis Rheumatol 66 suppl 10), no DOI/PMID; tier 1 assigned provisionally; Merck never published either study.
engagement.quote: The in vivo characteristics of MK-8457 were evaluated in the rat adjuvant- and collagen-induced arthritis models.
engagement.note: Rat AIA/CIA PK-PD modelling set the SYK/ZAP70 inhibition needed for efficacy; no human comparison yet.
engagement.judgement: Opening entry at proxy first-use year.

engagement.magnitude_basis: fraction of SYK-dependent readout inhibited (99% human basophil CD63 vs 69% modelled requirement)
engagement.confidence_note: ACR 2014 meeting abstract (Arthritis Rheumatol 66 suppl 10), no DOI/PMID; tier 1 assigned provisionally; Merck never published either study. The 69% target and the 99% coverage sit in two separate abstracts, so the comparison is paired by me.
engagement.quote: Subjects in both studies were randomized to MK-8457 100 mg BID + MTX or placebo + MTX for 24 weeks, this dose has 99% inhibition of basophil CD63 biomarker.
engagement.note: Rat PK-PD said 69% SYK/ZAP70 inhibition was needed; the Phase 2 dose gave 99% basophil CD63 inhibition in humans.
engagement.judgement: Readout differs (modelled kinase inhibition vs ex-vivo basophil CD63 blockade), but both are direct SYK engagement measures; scored direct because CD63 is ex-vivo blockade of an anti-IgE stimulus.
engagement.reason: Human PD coverage exceeded rat target

engagement.confidence_note: Opening date is a proxy: cevidoplenib entered Phase 1 for RA in Sept 2015 (NCT02717988); the K/BxN data were not published until Nov 2022, after the RA trial had failed, so the date the model was first run is not public.
engagement.quote: The mice were treated orally twice daily with 42 or 84 mpk of SKI-O-703 from that day for 9 days.
engagement.note: K/BxN mice dosed 42–84 mg/kg BID; no human SYK PD readout for cevidoplenib in RA has been published.
engagement.judgement: Phase 1 records (NCT02717988, NCT03315494) carry no posted results; the ITP trial's PD is another indication and was not used.

engagement.model: Rat collagen-induced arthritis, therapeutic dosing from peak disease (lanraplenib/GS-9876)
engagement.confidence_note: ACR 2016 meeting abstract (Arthritis Rheumatol 68 suppl 10), no DOI/PMID; tier 1 assigned provisionally as the draft does for the MK-8457 ACR abstracts (open rule question). Gilead never published the rat CIA study in full.
engagement.note: Rat readouts were ankle swelling, paw weight, histopathology, anti-CII antibody and joint RNA/protein; none was carried into humans.
engagement.short: Joint readouts only, no human PD
engagement.quote: Efficacy evaluations were based on animal body weights, daily ankle caliper measurements, ankle diameter (expressed as area under the curve), terminal hind paw weights, and histopathology of ankles and knees.
engagement.judgement: The Phase 2 (Kivitz 2018) measured VectraDA and TruCulture whole-blood stimulation, neither a readout the rat model used, so the model's PD was never tested in humans; the cell stays untested.
engagement.reason: No shared PD readout in humans

dose.confidence_note: Opening date is a proxy: first-in-human dosing began 2011 (NCT01446003), so the rat work predates it. ACR 2014 meeting abstract (Arthritis Rheumatol 66 suppl 10), no DOI/PMID; tier 1 assigned provisionally; Merck never published either study.
dose.quote: The in vivo characteristics of MK-8457 were evaluated in the rat adjuvant- and collagen-induced arthritis models.
dose.note: PK-PD-efficacy modelling in rat CIA selected the clinical doses; comparison awaited patients.
dose.short: Rat CIA picked the clinical dose
dose.judgement: Opening entry at proxy first-use year.

dose.magnitude_basis: SYK-dependent inhibition achieved vs required (99% vs 69%)
dose.confidence_note: ACR 2014 meeting abstract (Arthritis Rheumatol 66 suppl 10), no DOI/PMID; tier 1 assigned provisionally; Merck never published either study. Serious infections at this exposure are counted once, in safety, because neither the rat model nor the 10-day HV study predicted them.
dose.quote: MK-8457 improved efficacy in subjects with an inadequate response to MTX (Study 1), but not in subjects who failed anti-TNF-α therapy (Study 2), although Study 2 was limited to a small sample size.
dose.note: 100 mg BID exceeded the 69% target (99% CD63 inhibition) and worked in MTX-IR; HV margin (200 mg BID tolerated) was stated.
dose.short: Target reached, drug worked in MTX-IR
dose.judgement: Decision 16: the stated margin was 10-day healthy-volunteer tolerability (200 mg BID), not a NOAEL; the infection signal that ended the programme emerged over 24 weeks in patients and is scored as a missed harm in safety rather than as a dose block.

dose.confidence_note: Opening date is a proxy: cevidoplenib entered Phase 1 for RA in Sept 2015 (NCT02717988); the K/BxN data were not published until Nov 2022, after the RA trial had failed, so the date the model was first run is not public.
dose.quote: The mice were treated orally twice daily with 42 or 84 mpk of SKI-O-703 from that day for 9 days.
dose.note: Model reported mg/kg doses only, no exposure or occupancy target; Phase 2 used 100–400 mg BID and failed.
dose.judgement: Without a stated exposure target the RA failure cannot be assigned to dose; Oscotec said it would consider a higher dose.

dose.model: Rat collagen-induced arthritis, therapeutic dosing from peak disease (lanraplenib/GS-9876)
dose.confidence_note: ACR 2016 meeting abstract (Arthritis Rheumatol 68 suppl 10), no DOI/PMID; tier 1 assigned provisionally as the draft does for the MK-8457 ACR abstracts (open rule question). Gilead never published the rat CIA study in full.
dose.note: Sponsor states rat efficacious exposures match those in healthy volunteers (Dolton 2016 FIH); the exposure target was reached before efficacy was known.
dose.quote: PK analysis of GS-9876 showed serum exposure levels similar to those achieved in human studies.
dose.judgement: Opening entry; the abstract itself puts rat and human exposure side by side, but efficacy was unknown in 2016 so no dose status can be set yet. No tolerability margin is stated for the rat.

dose.model: Rat collagen-induced arthritis, therapeutic dosing from peak disease (lanraplenib/GS-9876)
dose.note: Patient exposure matched the HV exposure the rat was dosed to, DAS28-CRP did not move, and Gilead ran no further RA trial.
dose.quote: Plasma exposures of all study drugs were comparable to those observed in healthy subjects and historical data.
dose.magnitude_basis: exposure only stated as 'similar' between rat and human; no numbers in either abstract
dose.confidence_note: Exposure match is qualitative in both abstracts (rat 'similar to' human; patient 'comparable to' HV). Registry NCT02885181 results posted 2018-09-19 set the date; ACR 2018 abstract has no DOI/PMID (tier 1 provisional).
dose.judgement: Dose scored on its own prediction (rule v4): patient exposure matched the rat's effective exposure. Table row 'reached, failed, abandoned': the rat's effective exposure was reached in RA patients (30 mg QD) and the primary endpoint failed, so dose is contra derived from efficacy, counted once. Lanraplenib continued only in lupus/Sjogren's and later AML, never again in RA.

efficacy.confidence_note: Opening date is a proxy: first-in-human dosing began 2011 (NCT01446003), so the rat work predates it. ACR 2014 meeting abstract (Arthritis Rheumatol 66 suppl 10), no DOI/PMID; tier 1 assigned provisionally; Merck never published either study.
efficacy.quote: The in vivo characteristics of MK-8457 were evaluated in the rat adjuvant- and collagen-induced arthritis models.
efficacy.note: MK-8457 dose-dependently inhibited rat adjuvant- and collagen-induced arthritis (paw thickness).
efficacy.judgement: Opening entry at proxy first-use year.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: rat paw thickness vs ACR20; not on a common scale
efficacy.confidence_note: ACR 2014 meeting abstract (Arthritis Rheumatol 66 suppl 10), no DOI/PMID; tier 1 assigned provisionally; Merck never published either study. Registry records (tier 3) posted 2017 reproduce the numbers: ACR20 68.29% vs 24.39%, p<0.001; TNF-IR DAS28-CRP difference -0.52, p=0.308.
efficacy.quote: MK-8457 improved efficacy in subjects with an inadequate response to MTX (Study 1), but not in subjects who failed anti-TNF-α therapy (Study 2), although Study 2 was limited to a small sample size.
efficacy.note: MTX-IR ACR20 68.3% vs 24.4% (p<0.001) matched the rat prediction; TNF-IR DAS28-CRP missed in a terminated 31-evaluable trial.

patient_trials.quote: Percentage of Participants Achieving an ACR 20 Response at Week 12: MK-8457 68.29%, placebo 24.39%; difference 43.90 (24.52, 63.28), p<0.001.
Change From Baseline in DAS28-CRP at Week 12: MK-8457 -1.83 (-2.58, -1.09), placebo -1.31 (-2.01, -0.62); difference -0.52 (-1.54, 0.50), p=0.308.

efficacy.judgement: Scored same + partial: the primary endpoint responded in the MTX-IR trial as the rat model predicted; the TNF-IR miss is the same drug in a harder population with 31 subjects at week 12 after early termination, so it is recorded as partial agreement, not contra.
efficacy.reason: Rat prediction held in MTX-IR patients

efficacy.confidence_note: Opening date is a proxy: cevidoplenib entered Phase 1 for RA in Sept 2015 (NCT02717988); the K/BxN data were not published until Nov 2022, after the RA trial had failed, so the date the model was first run is not public.
efficacy.quote: In a model of serum-transferred arthritis, SKI-O-703 significantly ameliorated synovitis, with fewer neutrophils and macrophages infiltrated into the synovial tissue.
efficacy.note: Cevidoplenib ameliorated K/BxN synovitis and rescued anti-TNF-refractory mice; no patient comparison yet.
efficacy.judgement: Opening entry; the model paper post-dates the trial but describes the development model, so retrodiction is set false and flagged.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: DAS28-CRP change vs placebo at week 12 (-0.20 at 400 mg BID, not significant)
efficacy.confidence_note: Press report (tier 5) dated 2021-01-07 is the earliest public record; the registry record (tier 3, posted 2024-07-31) confirms the numbers and sets the status. Model paper appeared Nov 2022, after the trial; whether the K/BxN experiments predate the trial is not public.
efficacy.quote: On Thursday, Oscotec said its analysis of the topline data of the phase-2 trial showed that cevidoplenib, a spleen tyrosine kinase (SYK) inhibitor, did not meet the primary endpoint for the indication of RA.
efficacy.note: K/BxN synovitis cleared, but DAS28-CRP fell -1.15 at 400 mg vs -0.95 on placebo (n=163); lanraplenib had missed the same endpoint in 2018.

patient_trials.quote: Change in Disease Activity Score, Baseline and Week 12 (LS mean): Placebo -0.95; SKI-O-703 100 mg -0.91; 200 mg -1.06; 400 mg -1.15.
Lanraplenib (GS-9876), MTX-IR RA: Change From Baseline in DAS28 (CRP) at Week 12: 30 mg -1.26, 10 mg -0.78, placebo -1.36; p=0.978 and 0.300 vs placebo; filgotinib -2.46, p=0.002.

efficacy.judgement: Lanraplenib's 2018 miss (NCT02885181) is listed here for the record but changes no status: Gilead published only a lupus (NZB/W) model for it, so there is no arthritis-model track to score it on. Entospletinib in K/BxN (Káposztás 2023, 10.3389/fimmu.2023.1279155) is a later sibling-drug retrodiction on this track that again reproduced the mouse result; it changes no status.
efficacy.reason: Mouse synovitis cleared; patients did not improve

efficacy.model: Rat collagen-induced arthritis, therapeutic dosing from peak disease (lanraplenib/GS-9876)
efficacy.confidence_note: ACR 2016 meeting abstract (Arthritis Rheumatol 68 suppl 10), no DOI/PMID; tier 1 assigned provisionally as the draft does for the MK-8457 ACR abstracts (open rule question). Gilead never published the rat CIA study in full.
efficacy.note: Therapeutic rat CIA (dosed from peak disease, day 17-20 to 34): dose-responsive efficacy on swelling, paw weight and histology; Gilead's RA entry model.
efficacy.quote: GS-9876 demonstrated dose-responsive efficacy in the rat CIA model.
efficacy.judgement: Opening at first public use (ACR 2016, after NCT02885181 started 2016-09). Dolton 2016 (FIH abstract) confirms the rat CIA model was the in vivo efficacy basis for the RA program, so this is lanraplenib's own disease-model track, distinct from the MK-8457 rat AIA/CIA track.

efficacy.model: Rat collagen-induced arthritis, therapeutic dosing from peak disease (lanraplenib/GS-9876)
efficacy.note: MTX/biologic-IR RA, 12 weeks on MTX: DAS28-CRP change -1.26 (30 mg) and -0.78 (10 mg) vs -1.36 placebo; filgotinib comparator -2.46 worked.
efficacy.quote: Clinical efficacy of GS-9876 in RA was not observed, but GS-9876 was safe and well-tolerated over a 12 week period in patients with active RA on MTX.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: DAS28-CRP LS-mean difference vs placebo at week 12: +0.01 at 30 mg (p=0.978), +0.40 at 10 mg (p=0.300)
efficacy.confidence_note: Registry record NCT02885181 (tier 3, results posted 2018-09-19) carries the same numbers and corroborates the ACR 2018 abstract, which has no DOI/PMID (tier 1 provisional, same rule question as the draft's MK-8457 sources). Abstract-level reading.

patient_trials.quote: Change From Baseline in DAS28 (CRP) at Week 12: GS-9876 30 mg -1.26, GS-9876 10 mg -0.78, filgotinib -2.46, placebo -1.36; LS mean difference vs placebo 0.01 (p=0.978) and 0.40 (p=0.300).

efficacy.judgement: Paired by me: the rat model predicted efficacy at exposures the trial reached, and the primary endpoint did not separate from placebo while the filgotinib arm validated the trial. Not neg: the rat data showed dose-responsive efficacy, not a below-bar signal. This corrects the draft's note that lanraplenib had only a lupus model published.
efficacy.reason: Rat CIA cleared; patients did not improve

safety.confidence_note: Opening date is a proxy: first-in-human dosing began 2011 (NCT01446003), so the rat work predates it. ACR 2014 meeting abstract (Arthritis Rheumatol 66 suppl 10), no DOI/PMID; tier 1 assigned provisionally; Merck never published either study.
safety.quote: The in vivo characteristics of MK-8457 were evaluated in the rat adjuvant- and collagen-induced arthritis models.
safety.note: Rat arthritis models and 10-day HV studies were silent on infection risk at the clinical dose.
safety.short: Rat and HV silent on infection
safety.judgement: Opening entry at proxy first-use year.

safety.magnitude_basis: serious infection rate; model predicted none
safety.confidence_note: ACR 2014 meeting abstract (Arthritis Rheumatol 66 suppl 10), no DOI/PMID; tier 1 assigned provisionally; Merck never published either study. Registry AE tables (NCT01569152, NCT01651936) list pneumonia, bronchitis and enterocolitis SAEs on MK-8457 only.
safety.quote: A high rate of serious infections was observed leading to the termination of both studies suggesting a potential increased infection risk with high degree of SYK and/or ZAP70 inhibition.
safety.note: Serious infections (16.3/100 patient-years, one death) ended both trials; rat models and HV dosing (200 mg BID, 10 days) had flagged nothing.
safety.judgement: Counted once, here: infection susceptibility is a harm a rodent could have shown (host-defence models) and the sponsor's own 10-day HV study stated tolerability, so the silence is a miss, not an unshowable harm. The bleeding-time rise predicted from human platelet assays did not become a bleeding AE and is not scored.
safety.reason: Missed serious infections at clinical dose

safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (paywalled); human arm is healthy volunteers, not RA patients.
safety.quote: GS-9876 inhibited SYK activity in platelets via the GPVI receptor without prolonging BT in monkeys or humans.
safety.note: Monkeys dosed with lanraplenib lost GPVI platelet aggregation but kept normal bleeding time; dosed humans also showed no bleeding-time rise.
safety.short: No bleeding-time rise, monkey and human
safety.judgement: A stated negative prediction (no bleeding despite platelet SYK blockade) that held in dosed humans; scored on its own track because it is a different model system from the arthritis models.

safety.model: Rat collagen-induced arthritis, therapeutic dosing from peak disease (lanraplenib/GS-9876)
safety.confidence_note: ACR 2016 meeting abstract (Arthritis Rheumatol 68 suppl 10), no DOI/PMID; tier 1 assigned provisionally as the draft does for the MK-8457 ACR abstracts (open rule question). Gilead never published the rat CIA study in full.
safety.note: Abstract reports efficacy only; no tolerability, infection or bleeding readout from the rat.
safety.quote: GS-9876 is a novel SYK inhibitor which displays in vivo therapeutic efficacy in a chronic rat CIA model.
safety.judgement: The rat made no safety prediction. Kivitz 2018 reported no deaths or serious AE over 12 weeks, so the model's silence was never contradicted; with no harm to compare, the cell stays untested rather than same. Bleeding is scored on the existing cynomolgus track.
safety.reason: No harm appeared to test silence
